cues: At the dormitory swap, students left unwanted textbooks in an open wooden frame for others to claim.
An architect sketched a recessed alcove for the family’s novels, preserving clear passage through the narrow hallway.
At the bookstore, signed first editions occupied the entrance display, where visitors could admire their spines before browsing.
During the earthquake drill, staff strapped tall rows of reference volumes to the wall to prevent dangerous falls.
At the children’s museum, picture books faced outward beside a listening station playing recorded stories.
Travelers kept guidebooks in a camper’s narrow wall recess, easy to consult during long drives.
